findings: radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp: the gate is general: an integral leading group key, more than one thread, no DISTINCT aggregates. It uses no table, column, literal or row-count conditions. Input that is clustered on its leading key (loaded in key or time order, or join output that keeps probe order) is a common pattern.

The disjointness proof holds. Interior rows have keys strictly inside the chunk's open interval (min, max). After sorting, the neighbour check a.max <= b.min proves the intervals are pairwise disjoint. The predecessor search checks whether any boundary key lies strictly inside an interval. Together these mean each interior group comes from exactly one AddChunk call, and lookups are on in that call because SkipLookups switches the path off. So the main data has no duplicates across threads or abandon generations. Two chunks with the same (min, max) fail the neighbour check, as they should.

Multi-column GROUP BYs are safe. The split uses only the first column, so all groups sharing a first key land on the same side and in one chunk. ClusteredOrderKey keeps the order of signed and unsigned values (sign-extend, then flip the top bit).

Fallbacks are covered: NULL keys, unsorted chunks, SkipLookups, a thread starting after the global flag is set, more than 1M chunks per thread, external/spilled aggregation (rejected at Finalize), and missing uncombined_data. On fallback, the boundary data is repartitioned to the main data's radix bits and merged before the normal combine. The boundary HT's allocator is kept in stored_allocators, so aggregate states do not dangle.

Source phase: the main partitions reuse the existing single_ht READY_TO_SCAN path (finalize_done++). The boundary partition is appended in READY_TO_FINALIZE and goes through the normal finalize task, so finalize_done reaches partitions.size() correctly.
Minor, not blocking: memory used by the boundary HT is not counted in the sink's temporary-memory/external decision. It holds at most 2 groups per chunk, so it is small compared with the main HT.
